shikigami.form.value: A hound the size of a pony, with too many joints in its legs
A long-necked bird that never quite lands
A sheaf of paper slips that hold a human outline when they need to
A serpent long enough to ring a room
A low, heavy quadruped built entirely for pushing
Something child-sized in a coat, which nobody looks at directly twice
A swarm that reads as one animal only while it is moving
A pair of disembodied hands, unhurried and very strong
A toad the size of a cart, patient and almost entirely inert
A composite of three animals that does not agree with itself
A heron, far too large, standing very still
A dog that is the wrong shape in a way nobody can name
A boar with a coat like wet slate
A monkey with hands that are almost right
A snake long enough to go round a room twice
A moth the size of a coat
A hare that watches the back of the group
A carp that swims in air at knee height
An ox, slow, and not interested in being hurried
A crow with too many joints in each wing
A toad that sits where it is put and expands
A cat-sized thing made of knotted rope
A man-shaped outline in a good coat, with nothing in it
A wolf that is only ever seen in profile
A spider with legs like bamboo canes
A horse with no sound to its step
A bundle of hands, moving together as one animal
Something very small that is never in the same pocket twice
A bear, scaled down to the size of a child
A cloud of small birds that acts as one

shikigami.role.value: Scout — fast, fragile, sent ahead and expected back
Brawler — put between the user and the problem
Wall — exists to be hit, and is very good at it
Tracker — follows a scent, a residual or a name
Courier — carries things and people, including the user
Warden — holds a door, a corridor or a line and will not be moved off it
Specialist — one job, done better than anything else the user has
Support — does not fight; makes the user's fighting work
Scout. Goes first, comes back, does not fight
Shield. Stands where the hit is going to land
Carrier. Moves people and things that cannot move themselves
Tracker. Holds one scent for as long as it takes
Watch. Stays with whoever is being protected, not with the summoner
Finisher. Held back until the thing is already hurt
Distraction. Loud, obvious and expendable
Labour. Digs, lifts, clears, and is no use in a fight
Anchor. Holds a space so nothing crosses it
Courier. Carries a message and nothing else
Second pair of eyes, and nothing more than that
Executioner for curses only; it will not touch a person
Support. Makes the summoner’s technique work at range
Nothing, officially. It was the first one and it has tenure

shikigami.ability.value: Moves through solid ground as easily as air
Makes no sound whatsoever, including when it strikes
Follows a residual trail hours after it was left
Latches on and will not release until dismissed or destroyed
Bears the user's weight at a sprint
Divides into smaller copies, each proportionally weaker
Takes a blow meant for the user, wherever the user is standing
Speaks, in a borrowed voice, and negotiates on the user's behalf
Has a small cursed technique of its own, unrelated to the user's
Reassembles itself over minutes unless the pieces are separated
Carries a second shikigami inside it until needed
Sees residual cursed energy as plainly as colour
Holds a door, a gate or a gap against anything its own grade or below
Takes a blow meant for the summoner, wherever the summoner is standing
Changes size, within reason, to fit the job
Splits into three smaller versions that share one set of senses
Knows where the summoner is without being told, through anything
Drags something back with it when dismissed
Climbs anything, including the underside of things
Shrugs off the first technique used on it each summoning
Keeps a space quiet — no sound leaves it
Repeats a sound it heard, exactly, hours later
Is where it was looking a moment ago
Will not be perceived by a non-sorcerer, at all, under any circumstances
Hits harder the longer it has waited
Eats a curse’s remains and is stronger for an hour
Stands in for the summoner — orders given to it are obeyed by the others
Cannot be moved, by anything, while it has both feet down
Finds the way out of a building it has never been in
Bleeds something that curses will not cross

shikigami.summoning.value: A one-handed sign, fast enough to do mid-swing
Both hands, which means dropping whatever is in them
Its name, spoken clearly — a problem underwater or in a crowd
Drawn up out of the user's own shadow, which needs light to cast one
A mark drawn on any surface, which takes about four seconds
A few drops of the user's blood, which they are usually happy to supply
Not summoned at all — it simply arrives, and was presumably nearby
A hand sign and the name, neither of which can be skipped
A gesture small enough to pass for a nervous habit
Blood, not much, and the same finger each time
It comes when the summoner is hurt, invited or not
A struck match, or any small flame
Drawn in the air, in a stroke order that must be right
Called by its full name, which is long and private
Released rather than summoned — it is always present, folded away
A coin, spent. Any coin, but it must be given up
Three breaths, and it is there on the third
It must be asked. Not instructed — asked

shikigami.cost.value: Free to hold once summoned; only the summoning costs anything
A steady trickle for as long as it is out
Noticeable upkeep — fine for a fight, not for an afternoon
Heavy enough that the user cannot do much else while it is out
Cheap alone, but the cost rises sharply with each other shikigami already out
Nothing to maintain, but a hard spike every time it acts
Small and constant, like a tap left running
Nothing while it stands still, a great deal while it moves
Paid in advance; dismissing it early refunds nothing
A flat cost per summoning, regardless of how long it stays
Rises steeply after the first few minutes
Cheap, because it takes the difference out of the summoner’s sleep
Free, and the summoner cannot use their technique while it is out
Fed by what it does — a fight pays for itself
Borne by the shikigami, which comes back thinner each time
Nothing anyone has identified, which worries the people who have looked

shikigami.temperament.value: Obedient and literal — does exactly what it was told, including the stupid part
Sullen. Obeys, slowly, and makes its opinion known
Eager to the point of being a hazard
Will not be given an undignified order and sulks for a day if it is
Genuinely fond of the user, which is worse when it is hurt
Still testing whether the binding holds, and always will be
No apparent inner life at all, which unsettles everyone except the user
Professional. Does the job, offers nothing else
Fond of the summoner and openly unimpressed by everyone else
Nervous, and braver than it looks
Idle until the moment it is not
Takes instructions as suggestions and is usually right
Protective of the youngest person present, whoever that is
Will not be looked at directly and sulks if it is
Punctual to a fault. Leaves the moment its time is up
Curious. Has to be kept away from things
Hostile to every other shikigami, including its own kind
Grieving something. It has been like this since it was bound
Affectionate in a way that is slightly too much
Keeps count of what it is owed
Patient the way a creditor is patient

shikigami.binding.value: Gone permanently. It cannot be summoned again, by this user or anyone
Returns, but not for weeks, and weaker when it does
Reforms by the next day at no lasting cost
Destroyed, but what it was passes into another shikigami the user holds
Can be rebound, but it must be beaten again first
Returns on its own terms, hostile, and the user has a second problem
Gone for a month, and comes back smaller
Gone for good. There was only ever the one
Reforms overnight and remembers how it happened
Reforms, but something about it is wrong afterwards
Can be rebound, at a cost the summoner has not had to pay yet
Takes the injury out of the summoner instead, if they allow it
Comes back immediately and is useless for a week
Must be hunted down and retrieved; it does not return on its own
Whatever killed it can now summon it, until that is dealt with
Returns at the next new moon, no sooner, whatever is needed

shikigami.weakness.value: Comes apart beyond a fixed distance from the user
Will not cross running water
Holds one standing order at a time; a new one cancels the last
Weaker in direct daylight and knows it
Useless for the first few seconds after being summoned
Anyone who learns its true name can refuse its attention
Cannot be redirected once it has committed to a target
Cannot be hidden or veiled — it registers to anyone sensitive from a street away
Running water, which it will not cross unaided
Enclosed spaces — it is slow and clumsy indoors
Open ground, where there is nothing to put its back to
Its own name, spoken by anyone who is not the summoner
Fire, more than anything of its size should mind
Being outnumbered; it fights badly against more than two
Salt, in a line, which it treats as a wall
Distance. Past about thirty metres it begins to fade
Daylight, which makes it slow rather than harms it
Reverse cursed technique, which unmakes it rather than heals it
A direct question it cannot answer; it stops to think
The summoner’s own injuries, which it feels as its own
Being seen by a child, which it cannot bring itself to allow
